title: BlasPart: A Deterministic Parallel Partitioner for Balanced Large-Scale Hypergraph Partitioning
problem: Balanced hypergraph partitioning for large-scale systems (VLSI, HPC) must scale to thousands of partitions while maintaining high partition quality and deterministic outputs.
motivation: Modern VLSI and HPC systems have increasing complexity; existing partitioners struggle with balance constraints as partition count scales (determinism enables reproducible results for distributed workflows).
method: BlasPart employs recursive multilevel bisection framework for deterministic parallel partitioning. Level-dependent balance constraints improve efficiency and effectiveness. Parallel algorithm maintains deterministic output (reproducibility across runs). Designed for 4096-way partitioning on large industrial benchmarks.
key_novelty: Deterministic parallel hypergraph partitioner with level-dependent balance constraints for large-scale systems.
contributions: Recursive multilevel bisection framework with deterministic guarantees
Level-dependent balance constraint improving partition quality
3.33x speedup vs Mt-KaHyPar-SDet on 4096-way partitioning; competitive quality and scalability
limitations: Evaluation on VLSI and HPC benchmarks; applicability to other partitioning domains or dynamic graphs not discussed.
primary_theme: Deterministic parallel partitioning with scale-aware balance
